subject: Request: retention carveout and offsite snapshot hold (Helix Therapeutics)
messages:
From: DPO - Helix Therapeutics <dpo@helixtx.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: IT Compliance <it-compliance@helixtx.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: extended retention carveout & offsite snapshot hold

Hi Ben,

We are preparing for an upcoming regulator-driven third-party audit and need Redwood's support on two time-sensitive items:

1) A temporary carveout to retain offsite encrypted snapshots containing Helix customer data for 30 months instead of the standard 12-month backup retention. The snapshots are immutable once created.
2) An extension on certain operational logs (auth and access logs) to 18 months to support forensic traceability for the audit window.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Mark a named customer entitlement that prevents automated purge of the specified snapshots and logs for the requested period.
- Provide a manifest of the snapshots and an estimated timeline for performing a retention-hold.

We're aware this is an exception to Redwood's default deletion workflow — please let us know the technical and contractual steps required. I've attached our audit requirements spreadsheet for context.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
DPO, Helix Therapeutics
Maya.Patel@helixtx.com

Attachment: helix_audit_requirements.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: DPO - Helix Therapeutics <dpo@helixtx.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: extended retention carveout & offsite snapshot hold

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Ava (engineering) so we can cover contractual and technical requirements.

Quick answers up front:
- Technically we can tag and hold specific snapshot objects and mark them as "exempt from auto-purge" for a customer-scoped window; it requires a short-term override of our purge pipeline and a named exception record in our retention ledger.
- For logs, we can route selected streams to a longer-retention cold bucket, but that is an operational change with cost and key-management implications.

Requests from our side to scope work:
- Which snapshot buckets/manifest IDs? (If you can provide a CSV with snapshot IDs and creation dates that helps.)
- Which exact log streams (auth, admin, api-gateway) — please list the log prefixes or sample keys.
- Are you asking for a permanent policy change or a fixed temporary carveout tied to HTX-2026 audit window?

I've attached a short manifest (backup_manifest.csv) with how we would expect identifiers to be formatted. Kimberly — please advise on DPA impacts and whether Legal needs a signed SOW/Change Order before we implement. Ava — can you confirm approximate lead time for a hold once the snapshot manifest is provided?

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: backup_manifest.csv

Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: extended retention carveout & offsite snapshot hold

Thanks for the heads up, Ben & Maya. Quick legal perspective:

- Our standard DPA includes retention and deletion obligations that require us to delete backups and logs in accordance with customer instructions and our internal schedules. We can agree to a customer-requested retention extension, but it must be captured in an amendment (SOW or Change Order) that:
  - Identifies the precise objects/keys to be retained,
  - Specifies the exact retention window and termination date,
  - Includes indemnities/limitations for increased risk (e.g., storage of PHI/PII for longer than typical), and
  - Documents the subprocessor impact (we need to confirm no downstream subprocessor policy conflicts).

- Operationally, the requested 30-month snapshot hold is feasible as an exception. For logs, 18 months is materially different from our default — I propose we offer: 30 months for immutable snapshots, 12 months for most logs, and a targeted 18-month retention only for the three named streams you specified, limited to the audit scope. That reduces our exposure and is easier to document.

- Next steps for Helix: please provide the snapshot manifest and a brief legal point of contact who can sign an addendum. We'll prepare a short DPA amendment (excerpt attached) that captures the carveout language and required controls.

Attachment: dpa_redline_excerpt.pdf

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: extended retention carveout & offsite snapshot hold

Hi Maya — engineering lead here. A few implementation notes and timelines:

- Mechanism: we will implement a per-customer retention flag that prevents the purge service from deleting snapshot objects with the specified tag. For logs, we'll switch the named streams to our cold-tier bucket with a separate retention TTL.
- KMS/key rotation: if snapshots are encrypted with a customer-managed key, we'll need coordination for key rotation dates to ensure the audit window doesn't lose decryptability. If Redwood-managed keys are used, we'll exclude those keys from automated rotation for the carveout period.
- Lead time: once we have the manifest and a signed amendment we can do the following timeline:
   * Day 0-2: Create exception record and tag objects (small ops task).
   * Day 3-7: Implement cold-tier log routing and test sample retrieval.
   * Day 7-14: Run a verification scan and hand off a signed retention manifest to Helix.
- Cost: estimated incremental storage and retrieval cost ~USD 2,600/month for the snapshot set you described (ballpark) plus engineering time. We'll provide a formal estimate in the SOW.

I've attached our standard snapshot procedure doc and can schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough next week to walk through tagging and verification.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Engineering Manager, Storage Reliability
ava_chen@redwood.com

Attachment: s3-snapshot-procedure.txt
